content_record.title: Memory's hidden order: uniform sampling, not surprise, shapes what we recall
content_record.editorial_body: New preprint suggests the brain encodes all moments equally, but retrieval favors information-rich, interconnected details—explaining gist memory without costly feedback. Uniform sampling model outperforms surprise-based theories in explaining narrative recall. Mutual information, not surprise, predicts which moments are remembered best. Findings align with energy-efficient encoding and ancestral oral traditions. This signal is based on Efficient uniform sampling explains non-uniform memory of narrative stories from biorxiv. Read the original report for full context.
